payload.build_planned:
KILLER. The chunk machine was seeded at plan_build BEFORE the build - four chunks drawn to the M5 element boundaries, each with its realization kind and its dependency edges - and every one of them was walked and filled. c1 the sealed brief (E2), c2 the tappable card (E1/E3/E4's card half), c3 publish-iff-the-run-waits (the trigger), c4 say-what-happened (the record). Walked in the drawn order; c1 and c2 were drawn as independent and could have fanned out to parallel builders, and I recorded at plan time that they would not, because one agent already held the context and the coordination would have cost more than the concurrency saved. That is a judgement I am naming rather than hiding as an omission.

Nothing was built that the drawing did not contain, and nothing in the drawing was left unfilled.
payload.models_adhered:
The build filled the allocated elements and ONLY those. E1 the gatekeeper: config loading now feeds a per-announce transport. E2 the brief pipeline: engine/brief.ts, whole and new, exactly the element that was allowed to fail. E3 the summons: the card, its absolute URLs, its budget, its title. E4 the answer reader: unchanged except for the transport factory - correctly, since taps were never the defect.

NO NEW ELEMENT WAS CREATED, so nothing returns to the architecture gate. The one structural change is the one the prototype gate already ruled: E3's TRIGGER moved from the board's timer to the park seam. That moves an existing interface's caller; it does not add, split or merge an element, and the M5 allocation stands as drawn.

The two standing constraints held. Report-the-attempt is now literally true rather than aspirational (c4). Withhold-the-credential is checked on three surfaces at once. And the interface that M5 declared OPTIONAL BY CONSTRUCTION - the brief URL - is optional in the code: E3 builds its card whether or not E2 returned anything, and never asks why.
payload.red_observed:
Every new check failed before the build, and the reds were made to discriminate rather than accepted in bulk. First run-afe7d2f56851: all 19 failed together on a missing module, which proves only that nothing existed. Signature-only stubs were then landed - including one that deliberately reproduced the SHIPPED defect, answerUrl returning 'answer:<topic>' - and run-abcf53324e06 showed 14 checks failing on their OWN assertions, with R1 failing on exactly the string the owner's phone refused.

Of the 5 that passed against stubs, I recorded 4 as VACUOUS - true only because the stub did nothing - and named the failing twin that pins each one's real behaviour. The 5th, R10, passed for a real reason and was recorded as already built rather than counted as coverage. That accounting is in the observe_red evidence and I am not restating it as anything cleaner than it was.
payload.designs_realized:
Every requirement has realized code, and each is checked. R1 answerUrl absolutizes at send time (config keeps a bare topic - v1's rule). R2 the card carries a title naming iteration and gate, max priority, a distinct tag. R3 a three-action budget with the third reserved for the brief, sliced rather than assumed. R4 briefHtml + briefPage: the gate's own text, escaped, in a self-contained page. R5 AES-256-GCM with the key base64url in the fragment only. R6 publishBrief confirms the page SERVES before returning a link. R7 the ttl is the offer's remaining life, floored and capped at six hours. R8 every brief path returns rather than throws. R9 the park seam, plus the board stripped of its timer. R10 the transport is built per announce from freshly-read config. R11 the token lives only in an Authorization header. R12 every announce writes a record either way. Q1 is carried jointly by R8 and R12 - after an induced failure there is a card or a recorded failure, never neither, and that is asserted directly.

D1 remains the one design realized but NOT verified by me: the tap on a real device. It is this iteration's release gate.
payload.verification_green:
The engine's own verification state ran the full battery in the background and closed GREEN: run-86dadd78902a, ok true - the gate would not have opened otherwise. I am citing the engine's verdict rather than a pass count, because I attempted to read the run record and the read was denied; retyping a number I did not see is exactly the fabrication the ledger forbids.

What I did read, directly: run-3a83f64d9dc6, 26/26 across the new i8d suite AND the shipped i8 lane together - so the seven i8 tests still pass after the constructor sweep, and the change is shape, not behaviour. Typecheck clean at run-ac7f984817c4.

AND, beyond the battery, the chain was proven LIVE against the real store at run-a8e537c05cac, 10/10: a real brief sealed, published, confirmed servable in 687ms, then FETCHED BACK and decrypted from the served bytes with the key from the link's fragment. The host served 200 text/html (it renders, it does not download), the stored object contained none of the brief's words, and the page carries no external reference. That is everything the owner's phone will do except the rendering and the tap themselves.
payload.quality_ok:
Reviewed, with three things worth naming rather than a clean bill.

GOOD: the layout contract that broke my own earlier probe is now stated ONCE at the top of brief.ts, with both sides in the same file, so the Node/Web-Crypto tag mismatch cannot drift apart again. Both new guards are whitelists per the owner's law - 'servable' is exactly 200-with-text/html, and a store config loads only when all four fields are well-formed. The board's lost timer carries its reason in a comment so nobody reattaches it, and a test enforces that.

A REAL FIX FOUND WHILE BUILDING, not planned: NtfyTransport was SWALLOWING non-2xx responses - a rejected publish was reported as a successful announce. It now throws, which is what makes R12's failure record ever fire. That defect was invisible before and is the second instance of the blacklist-guard shape the owner named.

WEAKNESS ACCEPTED AND NAMED: the 'never serves' check costs 6 seconds of real waiting, because it exercises the full confirmation loop. It is the single slowest check in the suite. I left it honest rather than mocking the clock, and it is a candidate for the parallel-test work the owner already asked for.

DEBT: engine/connect.ts (the QR pairing) and brief.json setup are separate surfaces the owner must each configure once; nothing yet tells them the store is unconfigured, it simply runs at the actions-only rung. Logged rather than fixed here - it is enablement, not this iteration's scope.
payload.risks_acceptable:
Judged acceptable, with the residues stated.

ACCEPTED: the brief carries evidence content verbatim to a third-party host, encrypted. The host holds ciphertext only - proven live - but whoever holds the link holds the decision. That is the accepted-risk model the owner already ruled for taps, extended to brief content, and it is tripwired as se.raid-brief-exports-evidence-content for the moment evidence stops being ledger prose.

ACCEPTED: three action slots are all spent, so a future bless-with-changes must push choice-making onto the page. Recorded as se.raid-action-budget-binds.

ACCEPTED: rendering on the device is outside my reach; the floor is the two direct actions, which do not depend on the brief at all.

THE ONE RISK THAT IS NOT MITIGATED, stated plainly: if the summons ITSELF fails, the owner receives nothing and only the record shows it. A second channel is deliberately out of scope. So the honest ceiling of this design is 'reached, or recorded as unreached' - not 'always reached'. Q1 is written to that ceiling rather than above it.

And the risk that matters most is not in the code: this iteration exists because a leg the design flagged as unverified shipped unverified. That is why D1 is bound to the release gate the OWNER adjudicates from the phone, and why I will not self-bless it.
